096367d 2015-02-19 12:26:10 +0100 Marco Mascheroni: Separate COMP and CMSSW envs. Fixes #4300
Provides two new scripts:
  crab.sh: wrapper script that does scram unset env before running crab
commands. Also, if the command is a submit run the bootstrap script
  crab3bootstrap: executes all the operations that needs the CMSSW
environment saving the output to a tmp dir. Returns the tmp directory or
the error message in case of errors.

Backward compatibility is guaranteed since the bootstrapDone() function
is called to check if the clients needs to perform the CMSSW related
operations or the bootstrap script was run.

also refactored many parts of the client. We are providin now:
  flushMemoryLogger function that group the code used to save the output messages that
are stored in memory
  validateSubmitOptions to group the code that in the crab submit
command validate the command line options passed by the user
  setSubmitParserOptions to set the command line options of the client
submit command

title: dmwm/CRABClient issue #5187: Add src/*/*/python to the user sandbox
body:
# dmwm/CRABClient issue #5187: Add src/*/*/python to the user sandbox

State: closed
Opened: 2023-02-17T10:30:28Z
Closed: 2023-02-27T11:56:46Z
Labels: enhancement, HighPrio, In Progress
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5187

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-02-17T10:30:28Z)

### description

The change https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/pull/7865 stopped creating symlinks that CRABClient relied upon when the parameter `JobType.sendPythonFolder` is set to `True` in user task config.

### proposed solution

Shahzad on CMSTalk suggested to always add `src/*/*/python` and `src/*/*/interface` to the user sandbox [1].

We already add `src/**/interface` https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/b1d3d94c9ba5e2209f9687af21c34278e23804d8/src/python/CRABClient/JobType/UserTarball.py#L163

I suggest to simply add `python` to that line. A PR is on its way.

----

fyi: @rgerosa

[1] https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/missing-symbolic-links-in-cmssw-base-python/20403/35?u=dmapelli

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-17T10:56:05Z)

to be clear, after this change, the sandbxox will contain all directories named `python`, `data` or `interface` in the tree below `$CMSSW_BASE/src`. Not rescricted to `src/*/*/python`

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-17T11:01:16Z)

Dario, please update the documentation as well https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#What_are_the_files_CRAB_adds_to

## Comment (rgerosa, 2023-02-17T11:01:20Z)

Thanks a lot for handling this! As a crab user (not developer), I guess it would be also fine to keep the inclusion of `src/*/*/python` optional (i.e. that can be activated via the `sendPythonFilter` option). My use case was rather peculiar, as I am running multiple cmsRun instances inside a single job and not just the PSet one. This means that for most of the user the inclusion of `src/*/*/python` is probably not 100% necessary. However, I leave you the final decision of course  ... just wanted to add my 2 cents on the table :).

## Comment (belforte, 2023-02-17T11:04:36Z)

Thanks @rgerosa
I think we are safe by adding python subdirs under `src`, hopefully there's no junk in there. We need to have these lists because tarring up all of $CMSSW_BASE would bring in all sort of things.
In the end, if the tarball is too big, submission is refused and user has to cleanup, but we try to limit those occurrences

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-04-17T09:03:32Z)

EM framework requires that number of threads in the PSet is indicated as `uint32` but users may mistakenly use `int32` and the resulting pset will still be valid, but only use 1 thread.
See discussion in [MatterMost CPU Efficiency channel](https://mattermost.web.cern.ch/cms-o-and-c/pl/4hckcnwz3pgo7r5a9a9arua11h)

CRABClient need to check that number of threads is correctly indicated before allowing to submit a request for e.g. 8 cores where only 1 will be used.

## Opening post (kpedro88, 2023-09-19T13:15:14Z)

https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650 introduces general support for dash-prefixed flags in cmsRun Python config files. However, the entry for `pyCfgParams` in https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile#CRAB_configuration_parameters states "double dashes break things". I would like to clarify if:
A. this warning is just there because previously, double dashes could break things in cmsRun itself, so it warns users in advance to avoid many spurious issue reports, or
B. there is actually some problem in the CRAB client that prevents it from accepting flags with double dashes.

If the latter, this will need to be fixed.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-19T15:55:56Z)

I need to review this old topic, but IIUC it used to be the latter. Some problem with passing strings around.

## Comment (kpedro88, 2023-09-20T14:35:50Z)

Okay, once https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7888 is deployed, we can try some test cases.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-20T16:51:59Z)

I had a look and I believe all work is done in the client.
IIUC the PSet.py is loaded with the pyCfgParams arguments and the result
is saved as a pickle. Those params are not passed to the grid job.
So it should be easy to test.
If you have a PSet at hand which tasks args, I can give it a try. I tried passing args to a plain PSet, but they are happily ignored AFAICT.

Or do you @kpedro88 maybe mean that future versions of `cmsRun` will accept additional params with `-option` and/or `--option` ? CRAB is not prepared to pass user provided arguments to `cmsRun`.
If that's the need, I will look into how best to support it.

## Comment (kpedro88, 2023-09-20T17:03:50Z)

the new functionality that is supported with https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650 is a command like this:
```
cmsRun config.py --arg 1 --another-arg
```
where `--arg 1 --another-arg` are passed directly to `config.py` as `sys.argv` when it's evaluated in Python.
(to be clear, this technically works already, but requires various kludges, whereas in the future it will be supported natively.)

To me, what's in here already looks like it will work as intended: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/549c4e3b6158e8344315437d1d128f2288551d47/src/python/CRABClient/JobType/CMSSWConfig.py#L47-L62

https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650 introduces a few test configs like [test_argparse.py](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650/files#diff-7d2267b2acb976530035ac7bf5fab8dfc6b6fc39b533801e0268f0216c4fedaa). I can try to make a test submission with something like this in the next few days.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-20T17:21:17Z)

I guess my problem is that I do not understand how `sys.argv` ends up in
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/549c4e3b6158e8344315437d1d128f2288551d47/src/python/CRABClient/JobType/CMSSWConfig.py#L87 so am not able to say what will or will nor work and why. But I can certainly make tests.

I will follow up.

## Comment (kpedro88, 2023-09-20T17:28:00Z)

I took a similar approach to make `edmConfigDump` work with command-line arguments in https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650/files#diff-1909f065fd31286cb427528c31b4d73328a06edc51a0cf606941efe6cdb80f84, so it seems like it can work. (though it uses the newer importlib rather than the deprecated imp; the latter will be removed in python 3.12, so a migration is warranted irrespective of this specific issue.)

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-20T17:32:53Z)

that's not my code and surely I do not like `imp`, but we need to keep compatibly with older python versions as well since we use the one from the CMSSW release of the day.
I will figure out.

## Comment (kpedro88, 2023-09-20T19:51:22Z)

I think most `importlib` functionality should also be available in Python2.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-20T22:46:30Z)

oh well..
I tested [test_argparse.py](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650/files#diff-7d2267b2acb976530035ac7bf5fab8dfc6b6fc39b533801e0268f0216c4fedaa) with `pyCfgParams=["--maxEvents=8"]` on both CMSSW_13 (py3) and CMSSW_11 (py2.7) and it worked.
So it seems like that warning in the twiki applied to some "old" things at the time (> 5 years ago). I clearly remember that some users hit this double-slash problem and was solved as indicated, but details have not been preserved. I also do not know what to make of [this twiki](https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/SWGuideAboutPythonConfigFile#argparse), in particular the thing about the `unamed '--' argument `

My test  fails when using CMSSW_6 inside cmssw_el6 container with
```
Importing CMSSW configuration tpar.py
ERROR: AttributeError: 'Process' object has no attribute 'maxEvents'
```
which looks like `tpar.py` worked but the config is not consistent with that CMSSW version.
IIUC, we do not care about what happens with older CMSSW when trying to use this new functionality.

**OTOH**, I found that `pyCfgParams=["--maxEvents 8"]` fails, you need `--maxEvents=8`  or the "non-obvious" `pyCfgParams=["--maxEvents", "8"]`, I think this can't be helped as far as arg passing goes, it we want to be friendly we should insert the missing `=` or split multistring args in the CRABClient.

One annoying "feature" is that if the argument is incorrect and makes the PSet exit, `crab submit` just stops and exits w/o printing any more messages. I will try to fix this.

@kpedro88  I will wait for more testing from you, if all goes well we close this and fix the documentation.
Let's leave for another time to replace `imp` with `importlib` (`importlib.machinery` is not there in py2)

## Comment (kpedro88, 2023-09-21T07:54:31Z)

That twiki shows one of the kludges/workarounds that is currently required to use argparse with `cmsRun`. (CRAB isn't directly `cmsRun`-ing the config, but first importing it with `sys.argv` set, so this isn't strictly necessary in the CRAB case.) https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650 makes this unnecessary. Indeed, old versions of CMSSW will likely not support this out of the box, and that's fine.

`pyCfgParams = ["--maxEvents","8"]` is the "correct" way to do it, though the version with `=` is also okay.

I'll report once I've had time to run tests.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-21T08:29:38Z)

thanks
> pyCfgParams = ["--maxEvents","8"] is the "correct" way to do it, though the version with = is also okay.

moved to  TOP of list, now that I am on it I'd like to get it out of the way quickly

Can you let me know when https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/7888 is deployed in crab-dev? The full test needs this.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-21T14:05:38Z)

I had not realized the need, sorry. WIll do

## Comment (kpedro88, 2023-09-21T19:06:43Z)

My test was successful, so I think we can conclude that flags with dashes work fine.

However, to test with https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650 compiled on top of CMSSW_13_3_0_pre3, I had to make several unexpected adjustments to the CRAB config. Namely:
```
config.JobType.inputFiles = [os.getenv('CMSSW_BASE')+'/bin',os.getenv('CMSSW_BASE')+'/python']
```

I was quite surprised to find that those directories are not included in the sandbox by default. (https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42650 puts important contents in both of them: modified `cmsRun` and `edmConfigDump` in `/bin`, and a new python component used by the latter in `/python`.) Personally, I would expect that excluding these would lead to a lot of confusion.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-21T21:07:23Z)

we have
`sendPythonFolder` for the latter.  I am open to making it default,  so far need was limited and sandbox size always an issue. That's why it is not default. That's an decision taken by other years ago, as usual. Possibly things have changed and I notice that python directory is usually empty, so .. if user puts code there seems safe to assume that it is needed. Yet it could be simply some work in progress. Anyhow on such matters we go with what CMSSW folks say, of course !
Should we follow same line for `venv` folder as well and always include ?

The less config. parameters we have in CRAB, the happier I am !

I am suprised that `bin` is needed, never heard of it before. So far $CMSSW_BASE/bin is happily empty. Why does someone need a different version of cmsRun and edmConfigDump from what is in the release, testing new code aside ?
Anyhow.. .as before, if we need, we will add. But if a generic "you" is testing locally and have 3 or four versions of those binaries and submit a crab task meant to do other things, and hit sandbox limit, I fear you will come complaining.

I'd be happy to have a CMSSW tool which packages the sandbox for us, delivering CRAB from any responsibility there.

## Comment (kpedro88, 2023-09-22T07:45:51Z)

The `$CMSSW_BASE/python` directory gets populated if there are any folders `$CMSSW_BASE/src/Subsystem/Package/python`; it's how the files in those folders become importable by python (in the system path). Since CRAB imports and concretizes the config file on the client side, it isn't strictly needed for `cmsRun` jobs. However, for "scriptExe" jobs, there are many cases where it would be needed. (In particular, it seems inconsistent to me that CRAB always includes `$CMSSW_BASE/src/Subsystem/Package/python` folders in the sandbox, but not the `$CMSSW_BASE/python` that actually makes them work...)

Any compiled executable goes in `$CMSSW_BASE/bin` - only the latest version of the compiled executable, not multiple versions. Again, this is mostly important for "scriptExe" jobs. But for this particular feature, since it most likely won't be backported (because of the need to fix dozens of unit tests), a user might want to install a modified `cmsRun` manually if using an older release.

Perhaps the Core SW group can make a global recommendation for sandboxing. Personally, I keep everything except for `$CMSSW_BASE/test` and `$CMSSW_BASE/tmp` when making my own sandboxes outside of CRAB (but at least `$CMSSW_BASE/logs` can probably also be omitted).

## Comment (kpedro88, 2023-09-22T07:50:23Z)

As a reference, in my working area for https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/pull/42823 (which includes many packages, and also the other related PRs), `$CMSSW_BASE/bin` is 4.8MB and `$CMSSW_BASE/python` is 1.7MB. `lib` and `include` are the ones that get big (>100MB) when compiling a lot of packages.

In the full release CMSSW_13_3_0_pre3 on cvmfs, `$CMSSW_RELEASE_BASE/bin` is 48MB and `$CMSSW_RELEASE_BASE/python` is 3.6MB. A user could of course do something unusual that would put a huge executable in `$CMSSW_BASE/bin`, but I can't think of any legitimate way for `$CMSSW_BASE/python` to get much larger than that.

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-22T08:30:33Z)

> Personally, I keep everything except for $CMSSW_BASE/test and $CMSSW_BASE/tmp when making my own sandboxes

you will be suprised (but maybe not !) at the kind and amount of junk people have in $CMSSW_BASE,
from root files to CRAB work directories :-(

Anyhow, short answer is that with all likelyhood when Marco and others added the `sendPythonFolder` they did not have a good understanding of how it works.
I am happy to always include ` $CMSSW_BASE/python`

We can "try" adding `CMSSW_BASE/bin` as well since it is very likely to be empty unless when people know about it and know what they are doing. At the end of the day, if sandbox is too big we print a size-sorted list of content and hopefully user will figure out.

I wish we could easily allow for bigger sandboxes (current limit is 120MB), but it really depends on size x number of jobs starting at more or less similar time. HTCondor is already reporting long queues and failures in that area every now and then.

So I will close this as "nothing required"  and open a new issue about changes to what we put in sandbox.
Thanks

## Comment (kpedro88, 2023-09-22T08:48:31Z)

One more note for posterity: if a user wants to write their arguments exactly as they would on the command line, rather than splitting them up into a Python list by hand, they can do the following:
```python
import shlex
args = '--arg 1 --another-arg "my name"'
config.JobType.pyCfgParams = shlex.split(args)
```

The output of `shlex.split(args)` for this case is:
```python
['--arg', '1', '--another-arg', 'my name']
```
i.e. it correctly preserves quoted spaces etc.

will add to twiki

State: open
Opened: 2023-09-26T13:25:14Z
Labels: Low Priority
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5212

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-09-26T13:25:14Z)

When running crab client with an expired proxy passed via `--proxy` option, crab client fails with the cryptic message

```plaintext
Singularity> crab status -d crab_recover_20230925_162750 --proxy=$X509_USER_PROXY
Fatal error trying to connect to https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch:8443/crabserver/devtwo/info?subresource=version using subresource=version.
The server answered with an error.
Log file is /path/to/crab.log
```

maybe we can do better and check if the proxy is valid beforehand.

I will assign low priority because I know that this is usually not a problem, since the user is supposed to be responsible of his own proxy if he uses the `--proxy` option.

fyi: @novicecpp

## Comment (belforte, 2023-09-27T21:17:22Z)

ideally `--proxy` option is also meant to cover situation where not even voms-proxy-into is available. We could rather look into improving the message, in particular if `--proxy` was used.

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-10-05T15:52:32Z)

see
https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/issues/8737

Reporting conclusion here:

* CRABClient will use, on whichever OS it runs, the Rucio client for that arch as setup by
```
source /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/rucio/setup-py3.sh
```

* We will make sure that cmssw environment is not only changed during the execution of CRABClient commands (a forked subprocess in the end as per https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/master/bin/crab

* We will restrict use of Rucio python client inside CRAB to CMSSW releases where it works, and too bad for people stuck in SL6 era.
  * initial very simple testing indicates that CMSSW_10_6_x is OK, so UL is covered, thanks Matti.
  * but for using that we need to switch to using python3 for CRABClient in there (currently there's a problem with pycurl)

## Opening post (belforte, 2023-10-12T08:52:08Z)

Scope creep from “run jobs on the grid” to “and also manage my data”, which points to incorporating Rucio python client into CRAB Client ,
After discussion with Eric and Shahzad in [cmsdist](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmsdist/issues/8737)  and initial integration in [crab and crab.py](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5213) The plan is
 * do it for CMSSW_12_6 or later  integrating Rucio python client
 * later look into extending down to CMSSW_11 and hopefully CMSSW_10_6 (used for UL)
 * no support for earlier releases beside the current couple of cases where we fork a pyhon script (e.g. checkwrite)

## Comment (belforte, 2023-10-13T12:53:21Z)

about CMSSW versions:

* full compatibility with python3 starts with CMSSW_11 and Rucio python client can at least be intialized there. #5222
* CMSSW_10_6 has python3 but we use [FWCore.PythonUtilities.LumiList](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/CMSSW_10_6_1/FWCore/PythonUtilities/python/LumiList.py) which imports urllib2 which is not available in python3
* python2 client for Rucio exist, but not supported and quite old. I prefer to avoid it

Therefore we will use Rucio python client for CMSSW_11 and onward. We wiill keep dirty trick of forking a python script in a subshell for earlier releases where absolutely needed (I.e. code which is there already) and new functionalities will be there for CMSSW_11 and later.
Rucio calls can we done line this:
```python
if self.rucio:
    myself = self.rucio.whoami()
```

@mapellidario @novicecpp  feel free to comment and advice.
In theory we can pick `FWCore.PythonUtilities.LumiList.py` from e.g. CMSSW_11 and freeze it in our repo and it is likely to work with CMSSW_10 as well, like we did with `WMCore config` but I do not like to detach from the main repo in this way. Maybe we could switch to the frozen one only for CMSSW_10... where everything is frozen anyhow.  Maybe as simple as
```python
try:
    import FWCore.PythonUtilities.LumiList
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    import CRABClient.LumiList
```
?

In a way, this is done. Am waiting to close it is used in a few commands so we are sure there's no change needed.

with ref to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7933
THere is currently a mess in CRABClient.

Various commands return a value, even a dictionary which says `{'status' : 'FAILED'}` but this is never used, since the call is
https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/a18cbd0856b48ad4d2db728e613efd9ac9edc0f4/bin/crab.py#L143-L146

(of course I may have misunderstood...)

and any returned value is ignored.
We should rely on raising an exception in order to report a failure which e.g. Jenkins test can use (curent CrabClientValidation tests issues all sort of commands and simply checks that exit code is non zero !)

e.g. `checkusername.py` returns the username ! but AFAICT it is never used.

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/a18cbd0856b48ad4d2db728e613efd9ac9edc0f4/src/python/CRABAPI/RawCommand.py#L13-L15

I came to the conclusion that when command returns e.g. {'status': 'FAILED'}, crab CLI should exit with code 1, not 0.
(e.g. checkwrite fails to write)
So that we can check this an error in our tests, at least for the simple testes which we have now where we expect success.
This implies that
 * **ALL COMMANDS MUST RETURN A DICTIONARY {'commandStatus':'SUCCESS/FAILED'}**
 * Can not use key `status` to avoid conflict with what is returned by `status` command !

This an important change, even if very little code, deserves its own Issue and PR: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5224

title: dmwm/CRABClient issue #5248: crab report - raises exception when all the jobs failed
body:
# dmwm/CRABClient issue #5248: crab report - raises exception when all the jobs failed

State: open
Opened: 2023-11-02T16:27:46Z
Labels: enhancement, MediumPrio
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5248

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-11-02T16:27:46Z)

While working on https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/6540, I noticed that if all jobs of a task fail, then `crab report` refuses to compute `notFinishedLumis.json` and `notPublishedLumis.json`

#### example of a problem

consider `231026_133050:dmapelli_crab_20231026_153049` on test11. 4 jobs, all failed. (I killed the task after the jobs failed).

crab report fails with [1] because at

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/14c4ca79c704f1dea71088a3568cf937003597c9/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/report.py#L54

`reportData['runsAndLumis']` is empty, since

```plaintext
> curl -L --key $X509_USER_PROXY --cert $X509_USER_PROXY "https://cmsweb-test11.cern.ch/crabserver/devtwo/workflow?workflow=231026_133050:dmapelli_crab_20231026_153049&subresource=report2"
{"result": [
 {"taskDBInfo": {"userWebDirURL": "http://vocms059.cern.ch/mon/dmapelli/231026_133050:dmapelli_crab_20231026_153049", "inputDataset": "/GenericTTbar/HC-CMSSW_9_2_6_91X_mcRun1_realistic_v2-v2/AODSIM", "outputDatasets": [], "publication": true}, "runsAndLumis": {}}
]}
```

#### expected result

If I remove the aforementioned check in crab report, then `notPublishedLumis.json` and `notFinishedLumis.json` are identical to `lumisToProcess.json` [2].

#### discussion

I know that it is very unlikely that a user will ever care running crab report on a task where all jobs failed. And also a crab recover will likely be not necessary, submitting the same task again will be a proper alternative. However, I do not like that our client returns an ambiguous result.

What shall we do?

Keep in mind that `crab report` has this info [3], so it is not difficult to change the message to "sorry, all the jobs failed. You'd better submit a new task with the same config" if

- `reportData["runsAndLumis"]` is empty, and
- all entries in `reportData["jobList"]`  are failed jobs

---

[1]

```plaintext
Singularity> crab report -d crab_20231026_153049 --recover notPublished --proxy=$X509_USER_PROXY
...
Error: Cannot get all the needed information for the report. Maybe no job has completed yet ?
 Notice, if your task has been submitted more than 30 days ago, then everything has been cleaned.
Will save lumi files into output directory /home/dario/crab/local/z-submitted/crab_20231026_153049/results
Additional report lumi files:
  Input dataset lumis (from DBS, at task submission time) written to inputDatasetLumis.json
  Lumis to process written to lumisToProcess.json
...
```

[2]

```plaintext

Will save lumi files into output directory /home/dario/crab/local/z-submitted/crab_20231026_153049/results

...
Singularity> diff -s crab_20231026_153049/results/notPublishedLumis.json crab_20231026_153049/results/lumisToProcess.json
Files crab_20231026_153049/results/notPublishedLumis.json and crab_20231026_153049/results/lumisToProcess.json are identical
Singularity> crab report -d crab_20231026_153049 --proxy=$X509_USER_PROXY
```

title: dmwm/CRABClient issue #5274: Print all Publish Containers in crab status command
body:
# dmwm/CRABClient issue #5274: Print all Publish Containers in crab status command

State: open
Opened: 2023-12-14T17:02:55Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5274

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2023-12-14T17:02:55Z)

`crab status` command in latest version only print Publish Container that have the same name as `tm_output_dataset`.

![Screenshot from 2023-12-14 17-26-33](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/assets/2346664/173e39f8-f31d-4c88-a3db-2458cc38ff7c)

Now that we have multiple Publish Containers, we need to display all of them.
The info to display is already there in taskdb `tm_multipub_rule`.

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-12-14T17:06:50Z)

My proposal is print them when supply the `--long` arg.

The new version of `crab status` **without** `--long` (notice the `Publish container's rule` is gone):
![Screenshot from 2023-12-14 17-24-08](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/assets/2346664/0c26445d-753c-442f-9d89-499861d5f94e)

**with** `--long`, it will print Publish Container's name and its rule after Publication section:
![Screenshot from 2023-12-14 17-23-47](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/assets/2346664/7be70b72-3372-42dc-942c-2b02554cd8f6)

@belforte What do you think?

## Comment (belforte, 2023-12-14T17:31:02Z)

I'd rather add a new option than expect/ask users to use --long with task of >100 jobs.
But.. are we talking about one line for each output file ? I.e. mostly one at at most a handful ? Why not adding them all of the times ?
I agree that the crab status output is getting long. But suggest to keep looking for ideas.
Maybe add an option to list rules ? In the end rules on Publish container are not very useful, esp. if they have no expiration date. And one can simply to `rucio rule-info <container>`. Maybe one line about this ?

Anyhow, I would really really stay out of `status --long`

## Comment (novicecpp, 2023-12-15T04:40:38Z)

> Maybe add an option to list rules ? In the end rules on Publish container are not very useful, esp. if they have no expiration date. And one can simply to rucio rule-info <container>. Maybe one line about this ?

I don't think so.
I *always* use the rule ID as the starting point when interact with the Rucio system, mainly because it has GUI that easy to navigate around. If it not enough, then I will go to the CLI like `list-file-replicas` or `list-account-usage` command.
It also tell the users which rule is created and managed by CRAB.

.

About the `--long` I kinda agree with you. I personally do not mind having the longer output, and as the reason above, I still want to show both the container name and rule ID.

Maybe a new arg like `--show-containers` is the best option where we can keep status output short, trade-off with a little extra effort required from users to provide additional arg. We can also add more information to the output like rule expiration time or lock status summary.

URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5296

## Opening post (novicecpp, 2024-03-07T11:12:14Z)

In CI, we run CV/CCV in parallel to reduce the feedback time.

I usually have this error message when CI submit jobs (Runner run at 4 concurrents):
```
gfal-copy error: 17 (File exists) - Destination davs://eoscms.cern.ch:443/eos/cms/store/user/tseethon/crab3checkwrite_20240305_132750/crab3checkwrite_20240305_132750.tmp exists and overwrite is not set
```

This happened because current code rely on uniqueness of timestamp at the second level, which is not enough.
Here is how [crab checkwrite](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/f754471bc1511805bdad2ed3972fa15318c92c31/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/checkwrite.py#L89-L91) construct LFN:
```python
        timestamp = str(time.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"))
        self.filename = 'crab3checkwrite_' + timestamp  + '.tmp'
        self.subdir = 'crab3checkwrite_' + timestamp
        lfn = self.lfnPrefix + '/' + self.subdir + '/' + self.filename
```

As per your suggestion in MM,  appending the  `uuid.uuid4()` to `self.filename`  should be enough.

title: dmwm/CRABClient issue #5300: CRAB incorrectly following symlink in sandbox creation
body:
# dmwm/CRABClient issue #5300: CRAB incorrectly following symlink in sandbox creation

State: closed
Opened: 2024-04-02T21:38:25Z
Closed: 2024-04-03T19:47:38Z
Labels: enhancement, In Progress, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5300

## Opening post (kpedro88, 2024-04-02T21:38:25Z)

Linktime optimization is a new speedup enabled in CMSSW_13_0_X and higher. It adds a directory `$CMSSW_BASE/external/${SCRAM_ARCH}/objs-base`, which is a symbolic link to `$CMSSW_RELEASE_BASE/objs/${SCRAM_ARCH}`. CRAB is following the symbolic link when creating the sandbox and adding all the files in that directory, which can exceed the allowed tarball size of 120 MB. Instead, the symlink should be preserved to avoid duplicating these contents from the release base.

## Comment (caleb-james-smith, 2024-04-02T21:45:00Z)

For example, using https://github.com/cms-egamma/EgammaAnalysis-TnPTreeProducer, for Run 3:
```
cmsrel CMSSW_13_3_1
cd CMSSW_13_3_1/src
cmsenv
git clone -b Run3_13X git@github.com:cms-egamma/EgammaAnalysis-TnPTreeProducer.git EgammaAnalysis/TnPTreeProducer
scram b -j8
```
and attempting crab submission:
```
cd EgammaAnalysis/TnPTreeProducer/crab
python3 tnpCrabSubmit.py
```
is giving this error:
```
Finished importing CMSSW configuration ../python/TnPTreeProducer_cfg.py
Failed submitting task: Impossible to upload the sandbox tarball.
Error message: Error: input tarball size 120 MB exceeds maximum allowed limit of 120 MB
largest 5 files are:
sandbox content sorted by size[Bytes]:
27024496	external/slc7_amd64_gcc12/objs-base/ValidationHGCalValidationAuto.obj
21093232	external/slc7_amd64_gcc12/objs-base/SimG4CMSCaloPlugins.obj
 7683944	external/slc7_amd64_gcc12/objs-base/SimG4CMSCalo.obj
 7249312	external/slc7_amd64_gcc12/objs-base/SimG4CMSTestBeamPlugins.obj
 6601152	external/slc7_amd64_gcc12/objs-base/ValidationGeometry.obj
see crab.log file for full list of tarball contetnt.
More details can be found in /uscms_data/d3/caleb/KU_SUSY_Run3/CMS_EGamma/CMSSW_13_3_1/src/EgammaAnalysis/TnPTreeProducer/crab/crab_2024-04-02/crab_2023_Run2023C_0v1/crab.log
```

## Comment (kpedro88, 2024-04-02T21:46:38Z)

This seems to be caused by the presence of `config.JobType.sendExternalFolder = True` in the CRAB config. I think the symlink handling here should be fixed, otherwise this flag will always overload the sandbox in 13_0_X and higher.

## Comment (kpedro88, 2024-04-02T21:59:10Z)

In fact, it's probably a good rule of thumb for sandbox creation that any symlink pointing to a path starting from `$CMSSW_RELEASE_BASE` should be preserved rather than followed.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-02T22:27:01Z)

Thanks for reporting, and providing a nice solution.
The problem is that when creating sandbox the decision to follow or not symlinks is a global flag to the  `tar` command.  When I implemented preserving symlinks for `venv` I had to effectively build the tarball twice with two different options and combine. I am possibly simply ignorant here, but do not know how to make a decision on a file-by-file base.

Could this be attacked from CMSSW side ? When cmsRun runs, it knows about `$SCRAM_ARCH` and `$CMSSW_RELEASE_BASE`, why does it need a symlink pointing to the latter in `$CMSSW_BASE` ?

What is the role of the `external` folder ? I could handle like `venv`, will it do ? Or could users put any sort of thing there ? including links to files outside `$CMSSW_BASE` ?

## Comment (kpedro88, 2024-04-02T22:33:38Z)

Other things can go in `external` that would need to be copied. @smuzaffar would have to comment about why this particular folder from `$CMSSW_RELEASE_BASE` is symlinked where it is.

I think you'll have to do something similar to `venv` for `external`: copy everything excluding `objs-base` entirely, then combine with a tarball just containing the symlink. It's a bit clunky, but maybe at this point it can at least be generalized in case of future such issues. (i.e., find all symlinks that should be preserved, directly exclude them from the initial tarball, then append the preserved links to the tarball.)

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-02T22:34:23Z)

it is unfortunate that we did not discover this yet. Something is clearly wrong in our and Shahzad validation. He makes sure that crab submit works for every release :-(

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-02T22:42:36Z)

well.. Caleb's task was just "at the bar"
 `input tarball size 120 MB exceeds maximum allowed limit of 120 MB`

 with my simple test  I get a 107 MB sandbox. So we know why it was not spotted yet.

 @caleb-james-smith can you work around this for a while by removing
 `config.JobType.sendExternalFolder = True`
?

## Comment (smuzaffar, 2024-04-03T04:33:51Z)

Hi, in most cases contents under `cmssw/external` are not needed at runtime (unless you have setup extra tools in your dev area and in that case those tools should also be bundled in the sandbox).  Contents under  `external/slc7_amd64_gcc12/objs-base/` are for the objects file needed to build the Big Simulation plugin. These are only needed at build time ( `scram build`) and these are not needed at rumtime.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-03T08:58:33Z)

thanks @smuzaffar for explaining. Would it make sense then to put pointers to `objs_base` objects in a different directory ? I am still puzzled that `scram b` can't find `$CMSSW_RELEASE_BASE/objs/${SCRAM_ARCH}` and needs to be pointed to it.... but if a pointer is needed.. .why there ? maybe it was less work for `scram` but clearly it makes sandbox preparation more complex. "most cases" is not something that can be coded.

## Comment (smuzaffar, 2024-04-03T09:31:41Z)

@belforte , this is part of build rules each cmssw release use. It has been there since Sep 2014 (https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw-config/pull/28). I can fix it for new release cycles (14.1.X and above) but existsing releases (e.g already installed on cvmfs) or new releases for old release cycles will still use old build rules.

For crab, I think a simple workaround/soultion (which should work for all releases) could be that if `config.JobType.sendExternalFolder = True` is used then crab just exclude `objs-base` and `objs-full` from tar (note there could be two symlinks one for patch release objs and one for full release objs). Or crab can add a configuration parameter so that user can exclude any directory. All crab needs to do is to pass `--exclude` to tar command :-)

## Comment (smuzaffar, 2024-04-03T09:50:56Z)

@belforte , any specific reason to open tarfile with [dereference=True](https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/master/src/python/CRABClient/JobType/UserTarball.py#L116) ?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-03T10:34:24Z)

thanks for the tip Shahzad. Very good. I will do it.
You do not need to change the build process for this.

About `dereference=True` the reason is that users may have things in there which are symbolic links to other places in their directories, so that it works locally, but links would not be resolved on grid nodes, so we ship the destination file. Nobody thought at the time that some links would point to files which are already in the release or elsewhere in CMSSW_BASE. That is very old stuff.. as often the case I suspect that it was done because there was somebody with that problem and decision (not my me) was to accommodate rather than say "sorry pal, if you want a file, put the file there, not a link to it".

## Comment (caleb-james-smith, 2024-04-03T13:25:58Z)

Hi @belforte.

Yes, @kpedro88 suggested this workaround for my use case:
Change `config.JobType.sendExternalFolder = True` to `config.JobType.sendExternalFolder = False`.

Before this change, my crab submissions were failing for all datasets with this error:
```
Error message: Error: input tarball size 120 MB exceeds maximum allowed limit of 120 MB
```

After this change, my crab submissions worked for all the datasets I am running, for example:
```
time python3 tnpCrabSubmit.py

Finished importing CMSSW configuration ../python/TnPTreeProducer_cfg.py
Sending the request to the server at cmsweb.cern.ch
Success: Your task has been delivered to the prod CRAB3 server.
Task name: 240402_215012:caleb_crab_2023_Run2023C_0v1
Project dir: crab_2024-04-02/crab_2023_Run2023C_0v1
Please use ' crab status -d crab_2024-04-02/crab_2023_Run2023C_0v1 ' to check how the submission process proceeds.
```

## Comment (caleb-james-smith, 2024-04-03T13:31:39Z)

@belforte, I was also surprised that the tarball size was equal to the limit size:
```
Error message: Error: input tarball size 120 MB exceeds maximum allowed limit of 120 MB
```
My first interpretation was that it was not a coincidence, but that the size stopped growing once it hit the limit...
But if the tarball is created independently of the size limit, is it just a coincidence that my tarball is the same size as the limit?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-04-03T13:41:58Z)

it was a coincidence. tarball is created, then measured :-)

Thanks for confirming that you have a workaraound. Takes some pressure off having a fix in CRABClient. I will implement what Kevin and Shahzad suggested but will take time for this to be in production.

title: dmwm/CRABClient issue #5337: add support for CRAB3_CACHE_FILE=/dev/null
body:
# dmwm/CRABClient issue #5337: add support for CRAB3_CACHE_FILE=/dev/null

State: closed
Opened: 2024-10-18T13:18:10Z
Closed: 2024-12-04T20:01:42Z
Labels: bug, HighPrio
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5337

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-10-18T13:18:10Z)

ref. https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/adapting-usage-of-crab3-file-in-case-multiple-processes-trying-to-access-it/54334/4

current code does
```
DEBUG 2024-10-18 13:00:15.261 UTC: 	 Executing command: 'status'
DEBUG 2024-10-18 13:00:15.261 UTC: 	 Could not find CRAB cache file /dev/null; creating a new one.
ERROR 2024-10-18 13:00:15.302 UTC: 	 Unhandled Exception!
ERROR 2024-10-18 13:00:15.302 UTC: 	 [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/dev/null.1120937'
```

## Comment (ArturAkh, 2024-11-27T20:42:14Z)

Hi @belforte,

It seems like there is still some trouble when using `CRAB3_CACHE_FILE=/dev/null`:

```bash
[aakhmets@lxplus917 CMSSWWithCrab]$ crab resubmit -d /afs/cern.ch/work/a/aakhmets/private/htt_data_crab_nanoaod_submission_25-11-2024_prodreleasev12/crab/crab_data_2018UL_tau_Tau_Run2018A --maxmemory 4000
Rucio client intialized for account aakhmets
Found no jobs to resubmit. Only jobs in status failed can be resubmitted. Jobs in status finished can also be resubmitted, but only if the jobids are specified and the force option is set.
[aakhmets@lxplus917 CMSSWWithCrab]$ export CRAB3_CACHE_FILE=/dev/null
[aakhmets@lxplus917 CMSSWWithCrab]$ crab resubmit -d /afs/cern.ch/work/a/aakhmets/private/htt_data_crab_nanoaod_submission_25-11-2024_prodreleasev12/crab/crab_data_2018UL_tau_Tau_Run2018A --maxmemory 4000
Error: Please indicate the CRAB project directory with --dir=<project-directory>.
```

I think this is somewhat related to the following lines of code:

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/da79107c9f00eb1378c7da5ad57f46107f65c8d3/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/SubCommand.py#L666-L691

It seems like when not using the variable being set tu `/dev/null` the resubmission works as intended. Right after doing that, I end up with the error of a missing option, while I've clearly have added it in the command.

Would you please have a closer look?

## Comment (ArturAkh, 2024-11-27T20:43:25Z)

Submission and status query work fine with `CRAB3_CACHE_FILE=/dev/null`, though

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-27T21:07:23Z)

thanks @ArturAkh for reporting. I guess I did not test all use cases :-(
Will look closer

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-27T21:18:32Z)

I can easily reproduce, so should be able to fix.

## Comment (ArturAkh, 2024-11-27T21:27:40Z)

Thanks a lot, @belforte!

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-27T21:37:26Z)

the problem is that `resubmit`, like other commands, most notably `recover`, internally calls other commands. In this case `status`. But current code relies on the fact that crabcache file exists and is pointing to current task, i.e. the `-d <projdir>` from CLI is not propagated. By the way this opens to an interesting race condition in case multiple clients run at same time with same $HOME, which apparently have not surfaced so far.

I could easily fix `resubmit` into working. But at this point prefer to make sure that the `projdir` is correctly propagated in all cases, including when the initial command does not have the `-d` option (e.g. for `crab report`)

@ArturAkh let me know if you want a recipe for running your own version of CRABClient with just resubmit fixed.

## Comment (ArturAkh, 2024-11-27T21:44:36Z)

Ok thanks for the clarification, @belforte!

I agree that having the project directory properly propagated would be the solution to go for.

The issue is not urgent, so there is no need to rush :) Just wanted to bring it up since I 've stumbled across that.

In any case, I'd appreciate it very much if you would provide me with a recipe to run custom crab client to try thing out :)

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-27T21:55:49Z)

happy to do !
Instructions to run your own  Client are in https://cmscrab.docs.cern.ch/crab-components/crab-client.html#using-crabclient-directly-from-your-github-repository
All you need is to go to your cloned CRABClient repository and apply these changes:

```diff
diff --git a/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/resubmit.py b/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/resubmit.py
index 9178495..940a42e 100644
--- a/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/resubmit.py
+++ b/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/resubmit.py
@@ -31,7 +31,7 @@ class resubmit(SubCommand):

     def __call__(self):

-        statusDict = getMutedStatusInfo(self.logger)
+        statusDict = getMutedStatusInfo(logger=self.logger, projdir=self.options.projdir)
         jobList = statusDict['jobList']

         if self.splitting == 'Automatic' and statusDict['dbStatus'] == 'KILLED':
diff --git a/src/python/CRABClient/UserUtilities.py b/src/python/CRABClient/UserUtilities.py
index f6fd71d..47125dc 100644
--- a/src/python/CRABClient/UserUtilities.py
+++ b/src/python/CRABClient/UserUtilities.py
@@ -193,7 +193,7 @@ def setConsoleLogLevel(lvl):
         for h in logging.getLogger('CRAB3.all').handlers:
             h.setLevel(lvl)

-def getMutedStatusInfo(logger=None, proxy=None):
+def getMutedStatusInfo(logger=None, proxy=None, projdir=None):
     """
     Mute the status console output before calling status and change it back to normal afterwards.
     """
@@ -202,6 +202,9 @@ def getMutedStatusInfo(logger=None, proxy=None):
     if proxy:
         cmdargs.append("--proxy")
         cmdargs.append(proxy)
+    if projdir:
+        cmdargs.append("-d")
+        cmdargs.append(projdir)
     cmdobj = getattr(mod, 'status')(logger=logger, cmdargs=cmdargs)
     loglevel = getConsoleLogLevel()
     setConsoleLogLevel(LOGLEVEL_MUTE)

```

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-27T22:30:47Z)

Interestingly `crab recover` does not suffer of this problem when checking task status.

Because it already passed `-d projdir` as arg to `status`, differencly from   https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/9ada90b8ce350ab4bd64870692afa7f822333824/src/python/CRABClient/UserUtilities.py#L196

so:
- [x] give a better name (silenceLogging ?) to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/9ada90b8ce350ab4bd64870692afa7f822333824/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/recover.py#L711 and move it to ClientUtilities
- [ ] use it also inside  https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/9ada90b8ce350ab4bd64870692afa7f822333824/src/python/CRABClient/UserUtilities.py#L196
- [x] modify `getMutedStatusInfo` as in the patch above
- [x] modify all places where   `getMutedStatusInfo` is called in the Client to pass the `projdir` arg
- [x] look for any other place where a command is called inside another one (none at first look)

not so bad !

## Comment (ArturAkh, 2024-11-28T08:06:37Z)

Thanks a lot, Stefano, sounds like a good plan :)

I'll try the instructions for a customized client out.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-12-04T19:23:36Z)

logging in CRABClient is more tricky than I thought. Mostly if I put my hands in there I could not resist making larger chances to make things clear and flush to file more frequently. I better leave it alone and just add `projdir` where needed.

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-10-24T08:49:29Z)

when investigating https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/cmssw-crab-ci-tests-are-failing-for-last-2-days/55653 we discovered that https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5332 only works with modified TW's CMSRunAnalysis.py as per https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/8704

The problem is that after moving user's scram files in the `CMSSW_X_Y_Z` directory in the sandbox, the current TW code expands the sandbox "early", so creates a partial `CMSSW_X_Y_X` directory which confuses subsequent WMCore's `scram_project()`. The latter actually calls `scramv1 project` a.k.a. `cmsrel` and the problem can be very simply reproduced as follows where `sanbox.tar.gz` is the file sent to the job wrapper as e.g. retrieved by `crab preparelocal`

```
belforte@lxplus825/belforte> cmsrel CMSSW_13_3_0

    return eval('scram_commands.cmd_%s' % cmds[0])(args, opts)

  File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/share/lcg/SCRAMV1/V3_00_77/SCRAM/Core/Commands/project.py", line 71, in process
    return project_bootfromrelease(project.upper(), version, releasePath, opts)
  File "/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/share/lcg/SCRAMV1/V3_00_77/SCRAM/Core/Commands/project.py", line 116, in project_bootfromrelease
    area = relarea.satellite(installdir, installname, symlink, Core().localarea())
```

The problem surfaced when https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/releases/tag/v3.240930 was moved to `crab-prod` in IB on Oct 21.

body:

State: closed

## Opening post (belforte, 2024-10-25T16:12:18Z)

```console
belforte@lxplus825/bot> crab recover -d crab_20241024_131730/
Rucio client intialized for account belforte
step kill - task already killed
Command recover failed
belforte@lxplus825/bot> echo $?
28
belforte@lxplus825/bot>
```
Not only that, but `crab.log` has no useful information either [1]

In addition, that  makes ClientValidation test fail.

But in this case the failure is simply because there are no failed jobs to recover, everything was successful [2]

- [x] conditions that cause command exit must be logged, e.g. in places like this https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/d1457005ac93fd14ec53bf9911a32944b1dff69f/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/recover.py#L73-L74 Most likely leverage `stepExit()` for this as the comment already indicated. Unless @mapellidario knows some reason why this is a bad idea !
- [x] a message should be printed to console saying what's happened, it looks to me that `recover` never does this
- [x] we may want to reserve `crab` command to have a non-zero exit code for situation where something bad happens. Or otherwise rewrite ClientValidation

## Comment (belforte, 2024-10-25T18:58:34Z)

I decided to add a `logger.info` whenever there is a condition which leads to `FAILED`. It is more clear and flexible than do it in `stepExit()`

Now the existential question. If one types `recover` but there is nothing to do, do we end with exit code 0 ? Or with error ?
Already `crab resubmit` has a non-zero exit code when all jobs succeeded.

But we do not /can not check `resubmit` in ClientValidation.

I guess it has been one of the two:
1. change semantics
2. remove from ClientValidation

## Comment (belforte, 2024-10-28T10:32:03Z)

I am leaning toward changing current semantics and go for:
* if the recover/resubmit can not be done because everything was fine, return SUCCESS
* while still return FAILED if e.g. there's a request to get log or output but no job completed yet

## Comment (mapellidario, 2024-10-28T10:50:01Z)

> a message should be printed to console saying what's happened, it looks to me that recover never does this

> I decided to add a logger.info whenever there is a condition which leads to FAILED. It is more clear and flexible than do it in stepExit()

oops, I would suggest to add [1] to `stepExit()` in order to print messages like this [2], i must have forgot to do it myself.

in general, yes it is not trivial to decide what should be considered a "success" and how to communicate it. I will trust your style and decisions :)

---

```python
logger.info(retval.get(msg, ""))
```

https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/d1457005ac93fd14ec53bf9911a32944b1dff69f/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/recover.py#L405

thanks Dario !

## Comment (belforte, 2024-10-28T11:20:47Z)

how status is reported:
* a `retval` dictionary is passed to `stepExit` and `recover` returns reporting it to the caller `crab.py`
* in `crab.py` an exception is raised if `retval['CommandStatus']` is not `SUCCES` https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/d1457005ac93fd14ec53bf9911a32944b1dff69f/bin/crab.py#L137-L140

## Comment (belforte, 2024-10-28T11:30:56Z)

possible changes
- the `returnDict` dictionary needs to be documented
- `crab.py` could report and log `returnDict['msg']` if present (not all command report such key) ?
- could introduce  a new `CommandStatus` : `NOTACCEPTED` ?

hmm.. only the first one makes sense. And a comment in `crab.py` will do.
The "problem" is that `returnDict` content is free, other than the common `commandStatus` each command uses it differently. `recover` uses several other command which all return a dictionary which is passed along up to `crab.py`, even if not used.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-10-28T21:50:01Z)

There is no clean way to describe possible outcome with only SUCCESS and FAILED.
I ended up introducing a new
`retval['commandStatus'] = "NothingToDo"`
which can be used to exit the series of steps early, but will be converted in `"SUCCESS"` when reported to `crab.py`

The $X509_USER_PROXY is only used to contact CMSWEB, but actual submision on the server side will be done with credentials retrieved from myproxy.cern.ch

In addition, `role` would be set to `de` instead of `NULL`, and such a role does not exist ## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-22T14:17:20Z) Hi @ArturAkh until now the "logic" for VOMS FQAN has been "/voname/groupname/" I do not know if now we have a new use case (subgroups ?) or if the FQAN has been improperly defined. The original documentation says that FQAN format is `/group/Role=` with Role being optional. Slash-separated group names were not there. See https://edms.cern.ch/file/858263/1/EGEE-II-JRA1-TEC-858263-FQAN-Matching-Rules-v1.6_doc_cpdf.pdf pag 5 Which exact problem do you have because of this ? I have similar attributes in my proxy and everything worls. Is there any hope that we can instead stop worrying about VOMS groups and roles in CRAB submission ? All groups are listed in the user proxy anyhow. And I'd be very happy to simplify the code. Should we involve "those who introduced those /../../.. attributes" ? ## Comment (ArturAkh, 2024-11-22T17:29:08Z) Hi Stefano, We have a use-case where regional groups like `cms:/cms/dcms` are not assigned to VOMS certificates anymore, since this procedure was managed manually. This is currently not done anymore. At KIT - and I'd assume also at other German CMS institutions - we have used that for the access to storage. A way out of that would be for us the automatic assignment of the country group `cms:/cms/country/de`, which can be also added to the user proxy certificates as main fqdn. This assignment is e.g. visible in the new IAM CMS service: https://cms-auth.web.cern.ch/dashboard#!/home This use-case is not covered currently by group & role checks in crab, such that e.g. submission fails - at least when I have tested that last time with an attempt of having `cms:/cms/country/de` group as main fqan. In consequence, every new user at our institute would have problems to use crab and our storage at the same time, since they won't get `cms:/cms/dcms` anymore. ## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-22T17:34:50Z) but the proxy which is presented to your servers should still list all those VOMS attributes. Simply CRAB will not be able to force one of them to be first of the list. As far as I remember it was during submission of a crab task. ## Comment (ArturAkh, 2024-11-25T09:39:29Z) Here is what I see when trying to submit a task with `country/de` group in the main fqan `/cms/country/de/Role=NULL/Capability=NULL`. title: dmwm/CRABClient issue #5354: CMSSW_15_0 and above: Support for CMSSW x86-64-v3 as default micro-arch
body:
# dmwm/CRABClient issue #5354: CMSSW_15_0 and above: Support for CMSSW x86-64-v3 as default micro-arch

State: closed
Opened: 2024-11-27T08:02:50Z
Closed: 2024-12-11T16:40:49Z
Labels: enhancement, Done, On Hold
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5354

## Opening post (smuzaffar, 2024-11-27T08:02:50Z)

Hi,

 We are planning to make `x86-64-v3` as default micro-arch for CMSSW_15_0_X ( see https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/issues/12168 and [core sw meeting](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1482012/)). Though CMSSW_15_0 will support dual micro-arch stack (`x86-64-v3` and `x86-64-v2`) but `x86-64-v3` will be default.

  In order to avoid increasing the build time (and also crab sandbox size) in cmssw developer area, scram will only build for default micro-arch ( i.e. `x86-64-v3` ). If someone wants to use a `x86-64-v2` resource (e.g. the dataset they need is only available on site with v2 resources) then they have to explicitly enable dual stack build in their developer area.

  We would suggest that, for CMSSW_15_0_X , crab sumbit jobs to `x86-64-v3` resources by default. SCRAM can set some env variable to expose the available micro-archs support e.g for CMSSW_15_0_X and above

- Normal user dev area: SCRAM can set `CMSSW_MICRO_ARCHS=x86-64-v3` i.e. job should run only on `x86-64-v3`
- Dev area multi-archs enabled:  SCRAM can set `CMSSW_MICRO_ARCHS=x86-64-v3,x86-64-v2` i.e job can use both `v2 and v3` resources
- Dev area with multi-archs enabled but user explicitly want to use `x86-64-v2`: SCRAM can set `CMSSW_MICRO_ARCHS=x86-64-v2`

If `CMSSW_MICRO_ARCHS` env sounds reasonable then we can enable this for 15.0.X IBs but if you have any better solutions which can help crab using the correct resources then please do let me know.

```text
    client = CRABClient()
```

URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5413

## Opening post (belforte, 2025-09-16T10:17:43Z)

A bug was introduced in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5409

See: https://cms-talk.web.cern.ch/t/failure-on-crab-report-command/131905

Client now fetches runs, lumis, files list from S3, but for automatic splitting those files only contain the ProbeJobs at submit time. The tarballs on the AP are later updated by the various PreDag as processing and tails steps run. But remain local.

There are two possible solutions:

   1) for automatic splitting re-vive old code which wgets tarballs from WEB_DIR
   2) in AP, upload new tarball to S3 whenever a PreDag runs

Solution 2) is sort or "more elegant" but combersome, 1) is ugly but simple
Solution 1)  is a bit slower since for large tasks pulling files from AP is not as efficient as from S3

title: dmwm/CRABClient issue #5427: crab report undercounts files/events when UserFiles input LFNs are replaced by DummyLFN
body:
# dmwm/CRABClient issue #5427: crab report undercounts files/events when UserFiles input LFNs are replaced by DummyLFN

State: closed
Opened: 2026-06-27T21:57:27Z
Closed: 2026-06-30T09:33:51Z
Labels: bug, Priority: TOP
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/issues/5427

## Opening post (Kiarendil, 2026-06-27T21:57:27Z)

Hi,

I found a `crab report` accounting issue for a private MC task using `config.Data.userInputFiles` with `FileBased` splitting, 3 input files per job. The CRAB Task in question is https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/ui/task/260603_121045%3Akivanov_crab_Bfinder_2024_BuJpsiK_pix_2025_BuJpsiK_pix_2025 .
The jobs ran successfully and CMSSW processed all input files, but `crab report` reported wrong accounting:

```text
Number of files processed: 1
Number of events read: 960641
```

while an independent count over `processedFiles.json` gives:

```text
1193 files
2881134 events
```

I used e.g. job 1 for debugging. The [FJR](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/scheddmon/0137/kivanov/260603_121045:kivanov_crab_Bfinder_2024_BuJpsiK_pix_2025_BuJpsiK_pix_2025/job_fjr.1.0.json) is correct:

```text
mini_pix_1.root    events = 2500
mini_pix_10.root   events = 2452
mini_pix_100.root  events = 2385
ProcessingSummary.NumberEvents = 7337
```

But the [PostJob log](https://cmsweb.cern.ch/scheddmon/0137/kivanov/260603_121045:kivanov_crab_Bfinder_2024_BuJpsiK_pix_2025_BuJpsiK_pix_2025/postjob.1.0.txt) shows that all three input files were uploaded with the same POOLIN LFN:

```text
/store/user/dummy/DummyLFN_1, events = 2500
/store/user/dummy/DummyLFN_1, events = 2452
/store/user/dummy/DummyLFN_1, events = 2385
```

The original input LFNs contained a double slash, e.g.

```text
/store/group/phys_bphys/kivanov/Bfinder/PrivateMC/MIT//pix_2025/...
```

so I suspect they failed LFN validation and were replaced by `/store/user/dummy/DummyLFN`.

This causes two visible problems:

1. **Event count is wrong** because multiple input files in the same job are uploaded with the same POOLIN `outlfn`, so their metadata records collide.

2. **File count becomes 1** because `crab report` later strips the final `_jobid` suffix, so `DummyLFN_1`, `DummyLFN_2`, etc. all collapse to `DummyLFN`.

I find this behaviour quite confusing, when in general everything is fine with the task, but `report` misbehaves due to LFN problems for private MC, and does it silently, so I spent some time investigating. I would suggest either to make the dummy POOLIN LFN unique per input file, or warn/fail when invalid UserFiles LFNs would make `crab report` accounting unreliable, etc.

Best regards,
Kirill

[job_fjr.1.0.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29422438/job_fjr.1.0.json)
[postjob.1.0.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29422419/postjob.1.0.txt)

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-28T11:11:54Z)

Thanks @Kiarendil for reporting this. It looks like a bug that I should be able to fix.
Hopefully fixing PostJob to upload the correct metdata will do.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-28T11:30:38Z)

hmmm... fixing the PostJob should take care of **1.** above. But **2.** is sitll puzzling. I would expect to have filemetadata for just one input file per job, not 3, due to PJ bug, but then there should be 398 processed input files, not 1.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-28T11:58:59Z)

OK., when PJ creates `Dummy_file_<jobid>` it is effectively saying that all jobs processed the single `dummy_file` input, it add the jobid to deal with the situation where multiple jobs processed different parts (sets of lumis) of the input file.
To avoid this problem a different dummy_file should be created for each job... but this seems all due to some logical confusion. If the input file is in DBS, there is no problem because it will pass LFN validation, if the input file is not in DBS, there should be no need to put anything in inputfilemetadata.

While handling the `//` is easy, I need to worry about the situation when UserInputFiles is a list of PFN's which will never pass LFN validation.

Need some time to reconstruct the full logical chain from PJ to crab report and to Publisher.

## Comment (Kiarendil, 2026-06-28T12:04:21Z)

Maybe it is easier to just forbid user to submit CRAB task, when UserFiles do not pass LFN validation? Or there could be cases when it can be useful?

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-28T13:50:45Z)

The idea was that user can also provide PFN's like `root://.....` or `dcap:...` or any file locally mounted at the site where jobs run, regardless of being in `/cms` directory tree.
Of course as long as all data are accessible via `xrootd` and are places inside CMS name space, LFN will suffice. But having this feature may still be good.

Besides, even if CRAB is end-of-life now, I prefer to take this chance to  bring clarity of design where "what should happen" is clearly spelled in English and code is consistent with that.
I nothing else, it will be "use case description for next WMS tool"

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-28T15:12:22Z)

Trying to find out how dummy file names make their way into `crab report`:

First:
```python
dictresult, status, _ = server.get(api=self.defaultApi, data={'workflow': self.cachedinfo['RequestName'], 'subresource': 'report2'})
```
which gives things like:
```
(Pdb) pprint(dictresult['result',0,'runsAndLumis','1'])
[{'events': 0,
  'lfn': '/store/user/kivanov/Bfinder/MC/BuJpsiK_pix_2025/2024/CRAB_UserFiles/CRAB3_Bfinder/260603_121045/0000/BFinder_pix_1.root',
  'parents': '[]',
  'runlumi': '{}',
  'type': 'TFILE'},
 {'events': 2500,
  'lfn': '/store/user/dummy/DummyLFN_1',
  'parents': '[]',
  'runlumi': "{'1': {'1': 'None'}}",
  'type': 'POOLIN'}]
(Pdb)
```
which lists both output (as TFILE) and input (as POOLIN)....

this is then copied into `reportData['processedRunsAndLumis',jobId]` (jobId as a string)

Then input file list is retrieved from S3, the tarball contains one file per job like
```console
belforte@lxplus813/IF> cat job_input_file_list_1.txt |jq
[
  "/store/group/phys_bphys/kivanov/Bfinder/PrivateMC/MIT//pix_2025/BuJpsiK_pix_2025/crab_BuJpsiK_pix_2025/260602_155211/0000/mini_pix_1.root",
  "/store/group/phys_bphys/kivanov/Bfinder/PrivateMC/MIT//pix_2025/BuJpsiK_pix_2025/crab_BuJpsiK_pix_2025/260602_155211/0000/mini_pix_10.root",
  "/store/group/phys_bphys/kivanov/Bfinder/PrivateMC/MIT//pix_2025/BuJpsiK_pix_2025/crab_BuJpsiK_pix_2025/260602_155211/0000/mini_pix_100.root"
]
belforte@lxplus813/IF>
```
Those becomes a list of dictionaries in `reportData['filesToProcess']`

The number of processed input files is then computed based on the `POOLIN` files
```python
        numFilesProcessed = _getNumFiles(reportData['processedRunsAndLumis'], 'POOLIN')
```
but `_getNumFiles` has
```python
 # the split is done to remove the jobnumber at the end of the input file lfn
      files.add('_'.join(rep['lfn'].split('_')[:-1]))
```

So `crab report` should be fixed by fixing PostJob. I will anyhow tests this.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-28T15:18:51Z)

@Kiarendil I'd like to test re-running PostJob on your task to make sure I understand the code flow and test a fix. Am I free to mess with your task ? I do not expect anything to change, but it could be that a new `crab report` will give different (and yet not correct) results.
Do you still have a use for the json files in `crab_Bfinder_2024_BuJpsiK_pix_2025_BuJpsiK_pix_2025/results` ?

## Comment (Kiarendil, 2026-06-28T15:22:17Z)

Sure, please mess whatever you need :)

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-28T16:31:19Z)

Note: I do not like that the numbers printed by `crab report` to stdout are not consistent with the content of `results/processedFiles.json`. Ideally things should come from same source, whether they are right or wrong.
Maybe the input file metadata should be ignored here.

But it seems that input file metadata is the only place where we record the number of processed events.

The ideal solution would be that the statistics for `crab report` are compute by parsing the FJR's of successful jobs, i.e. in the AP, then added to the status_cache.json file which is read by the client. We have some schizophrenic approach where something comes form DB, but still crab report need a working crab status ... so if AP's WEB_DIR becomes unavailable we are stuck in any case.

I am making the dummy file name in the metadata a valid LFN format yet unique for every unique input file name. That should solve this, but leaves the schizophrenia.

## Comment (belforte, 2026-06-29T09:20:45Z)

The PostJob change in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/pull/9337 will fix this (see https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/9336#issuecomment-4830837779)

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-01-24T13:28:40Z)

Related to https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7493

### status

tested

### description

submit --dryrun needs to run for at least 25s in order not to make its estimates based on very few small events. If the first dryrun attempt is too short, the same cmsRun command is called again, with an increasing number of events. with this commit, every trial reports how long it took and how many events the next trial will process.

As suggested by stefano in https://github.com/dmwm/CRABServer/issues/7493#issuecomment-1398722319, we have

```plaintext

^CKeyboard Interrupted
Log file is [...]/crab.log
```

title: dmwm/CRABClient PR #5250: crab recover - new command
body:
# dmwm/CRABClient pull request #5250: crab recover - new command

State: closed
Opened: 2023-11-10T12:24:12Z
Closed: 2023-12-01T13:14:15Z
Merged: 2023-12-01T13:14:15Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/pull/5250

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2023-11-10T12:24:12Z)

### scope

First implementation of automatic submission of a recovery task, without the need for users to follow instructions at [1]

how to trigger this new functionality: from crab client, run `crab recover --task=<taskname>`.

This command **supports** the recovery task for a task that

- has jobtype analysis
- uses a splitting algorithm that is aware of lumisections (automatic, lumibased, eventawarelumibased)

This command supports, but we have **not thoroughly** tested

- recover of a task submitted with automatic splitting [**]. User are encouraged to use it, but some extra caution may be needed.

does **not** support recovery of a task

- filebased splitting: will be done at a later stage
- privatemc: makes little sense, a user can just submit a new task.

### status

- [x] needs a reivew
- [x] ~~need to suppress debug logs, which may be useful for the review~~

changes  since out chat on 2023-11-10 afternoon:

- (functional) I changed the default strategy to "notPublished"
- (functional) killed is a final state. cooloff is a transient state, held is a transient state
- (functional) improve error message when crab report outputs are empty [5]
- (functional) improved stdout log messages
- (technical) crab remake does not need to be changed. It was a merge error on my side.
    - I needed to account for this `if` not having a return [4]
- (technical) suppress debug messages
- (technical) use exceptions, not asserts, suggested by @novicecpp
- (technical) jobtype Recover.py load task configuration only once, not twice as copycat.py needs to do.

### details

Entrypoint: the new file `src/python/CRABClient/Commands/recover.py`.

Since I needed to convert a manual list of actions into a crab client command, I opted for a procedural approach. I grouped the manual actions in steps, I created a function `step*` for very step. Some steps have side effects.

apart from technicalities, we should focus our attention to

- how do we decide that the original task is actually in a final state and not in a transient state? I am not sure that the current policy can identify a static automatic splitting task.

technical details that may be not trivial to grasp

- i take the task config, pset and script exe from the original sandboxes
- I override task config options via crab submit command line options, see [2]
- I use the "Recover" jobtype, which means that the command "submit.py" will call at [3]  the new file `src/python/CRABClient/JobType/Recover.py`
- `src/python/CRABClient/JobType/Recover.py` is a modification of `src/python/CRABClient/JobType/CopyOfTask.py`, which is the original copycat implementation by @novicecpp
    - Since I do not want to get credits for something I did not do, I can remove that file from this PR before merging. It is here just because it will be easier to compare the two when reviewing
- differences between mine and Wa's implementation
    - Wa's copyoftask assumes that the task that needs to be copied is specified in the task config
    - while in this PR we want to specify the original task name in the command line.
    - Wa did not need to change the lumimask
    - Wa did not need to care about publishing the output in the same DBS dataset as the original task

---

[**]

when we recover a task that has been submitted with automatic splitting we can have

- some jobs are still in a transient state. crab recover will kill the task, but will not submit the recovery task. The user will need to run crab recover again
- all jobs finished and some failed. crab recover will kill the task (disabling resubmission in the future), will check all job user status, will proceed with crab submit
- all the jobs that have been submitted already are in a final state, but not all jobs have been submitted yet. crab recover will kill the task, will check that all jobs in the schedd are in a final state, then will proceed with crab submit
    - danger: since crab recover does not wait, there is a small possibility that some new jobs are submitted between the execution of crab kill and crab report.
    - however, TW should kill all those jobs soon enough not to have them create any new output file. I am confident that this will not cause any problem

[1] https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CRAB3FAQ#Recovery_task
[2] https://twiki.cern.ch/twiki/bin/view/CMSPublic/CRAB3ConfigurationFile#Passing_CRAB_configuration_param
[3] https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/0edda22ce9af3ff76a41bc25fecb269762f54a6f/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/submit.py#L107

[4] https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/blob/a18cbd0856b48ad4d2db728e613efd9ac9edc0f4/src/python/CRABClient/Commands/remake.py#L23

[5]

- `231110_180452:dmapelli_crab_test_20231110_190450` : original failing task. 3/5 jobs published
- recovered by `231110_185245:dmapelli_crab_20231110_195244` (crab report created `notPublished.json`). 2/2 jobs published
- recovered again by `231110_190318:dmapelli_crab_20231110_200317`. bug, should not have been submitted. 1/2 jobs published
- recovered again by `231110_194043:dmapelli_crab_20231110_204042`. bug, should not have been submitted. 2/2 jobs published
- bug fixed, but now crab recover fails with a cryptic message that I am not really sure how to improve. I will need to sleep on this.

## Opening post (mapellidario, 2024-05-14T14:23:40Z)

fixes #5314

### status

tested on my laptop, but i have a small question before merging

### solution

This PR serves multiple purposes:

- make bash autocompletion respect the order at which we provide the commands. see the use of `-o nosort` in `complete -F _UseCrab -o filenames -o nosort crab`
- do not edit the `etc/crab-bashpcimpletion.sh` directly, generate it programmatically from `scripts/generate-completions.py`
  - make `generate-completions.py` work with python3
    - use `importlib` instead of  `imp`
  - make `generate-completions.py` generate the completion in our desired ordering, see the use of the `weights` variable.

open questions:

- [ ] I did not replicate to the variable `weights` the exact sorting that we have now yet.
  - take a look at `etc/crab-bash-completion.sh` line 26. the order here is what bash shows when you press `crab <tab><tab>` (the order of line 32 will be the same as line 26)
  - what is the exact order that we want here?

### comment

I decided to revamp the `generate_completion.py` script because I did not want to think about adding manually all the new commands introduced with `crab recover` :)

title: dmwm/CRABClient PR #5350: Python3.12 support: Use importlib instead of deprecated imp module
body:
# dmwm/CRABClient pull request #5350: Python3.12 support: Use importlib instead of deprecated imp module

State: closed
Opened: 2024-11-21T10:40:26Z
Closed: 2024-11-21T11:17:16Z
Merged: 2024-11-21T11:17:16Z
URL: https://github.com/dmwm/CRABClient/pull/5350

## Opening post (smuzaffar, 2024-11-21T10:40:26Z)

`imp` module has been deprecated and removed in `python 3.12`. This PR proposes to uses `importlib` for `python 3.12` e.g in `CMSSW_14_2_PY3_12_X` IBs. It should not break crab client for CMSSW release with `python version < 3.12`.

This requires newer WMCore specially change in [WMCore/Configuration.py](https://github.com/dmwm/WMCore/pull/11530/files#diff-ae418221154baa0ba96bdcf0566fde2fccf43a95d289f435f28c45e2a0552f1b) .

Note that using this I was able to submit crab job for CMSSW_14_2_PY312_X but they [fail on crab server side](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/0195/cmsbot/241121_102531:cmsbot_crab_Jenkins_CMSSW_14_2_PY312_X_2024-11-20-2300_el8_amd64_gcc12_123400/job_out.1.0.txt) as due to usage of `imp` in crab server code. So in order to fully support python 3.12 crab jobs, one needs to update crab server code too

## Comment (cmsdmwmbot, 2024-11-21T10:42:01Z)

Can one of the admins verify this patch?

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-21T11:05:12Z)

:bow:
great work @smuzaffar . As always.
I did not know that we are moving toward python 3.12.  And will be very happy to future-proof server code as well, even if currently we run it in a python3.8 debian container.

But am very puzzled by the run-time error in y [fail on crab server side](https://cmsweb.cern.ch:8443/scheddmon/0195/cmsbot/241121_102531:cmsbot_crab_Jenkins_CMSSW_14_2_PY312_X_2024-11-20-2300_el8_amd64_gcc12_123400/job_out.1.0.txt) since at first sight the traceback indicates presence of WMCore's /cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cc8_amd64_gcc9 environment inside cmsRun execution, which both WMCore and CRAB worked hard to separate.

That still needs to be understood.
Hopefully this is not super-urgent and I can look at it after I am done with current work ?
We can surely get this change into the client in the meanwhile and check other commands.

I will open issues in CRABServer repo for the work on that side.

## Comment (belforte, 2024-11-21T11:17:11Z)

LGTM

## Comment (smuzaffar, 2024-11-21T14:56:33Z)

thanks @belforte.
The failure [a] is due to the usage of `past.builtins` in [FWCore/ParameterSet/python/Types.py](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/FWCore/ParameterSet/python/Types.py#L6). `past.builtins` is provided via `future` package which is loaded from `/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cc8_amd64_gcc9/external/py3-future/0.18.2/lib/python3.8/site-packages` as something (crab or wmcore) sets `PYTHONPATH` to `/srv/WMCore.zip:/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/cc8_amd64_gcc9/external/py3-future/0.18.2/lib/python3.8/site-packages`.

I will fix cmssw FW code to not use  `past.builtins`  which will allow us to run crab tests. I proper fix/workaround  might be to not source `py3-future` for python 3.12 and above

[a]

## Opening post (Lorenzov1999, 2025-09-05T09:01:41Z)

This PR weakens the conditions of the RegEx used to parse HTTP responses from the server (that at the moment requires a ".<minor version>" after HTTP), avoiding failures for HTTP2, which:
- may not have minor version
- don't provide reason next to the status code

A status code is generated from the http library, when missing.

Example outputs:
``` bash
2025-09-05 10:53 lvalenti@lxplus9106:~$ curl -v --http1.1 --cert /tmp/x509up_u156194 --key /tmp/x509up_u156194 -k https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/prod/info 2>&1 1>/dev/null | python3 parser.py
HTTP code=200, reason='OK'
2025-09-05 10:53 lvalenti@lxplus9106:~$ curl -v --http1.1 --cert /tmp/x509up_u156194 --key /tmp/x509up_u156194 -k https://cmsweb.cern.ch/crabserver/prod/fakeendpoint 2>&1 1>/dev/null | python3 parser.py
HTTP code=404, reason='Not Found'

HTTP code=200, reason='OK'
```

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-09-05T11:39:30Z)

Thank you @Lorenzov1999 for reaching out!

We've double checked & tested both regEx back then [1] and your new relaxed but generic & robust one [2].

We can confirm our shortcoming, and see no obvious reasons not to support all HTTP versions. (This chunk of code seems to be only place sensitive to http version)

So, I think we could safely merged this PR. @belforte

Again. Thank you so much for your thoughtful patch and all these clarifications!

[1]
```
output: HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found -- extracted --> ['404', 'Not Found'], reason: Not Found
output: HTTP/1.1 200 OK -- extracted --> ['200', 'OK'], reason: OK
can't matched: HTTP/2 404
can't matched: HTTP/2 200
```
[2] The proposed extracting into `parts`, looks good and quite robust via filling missing reasons messages when not available.
```
crab ❯ python test_regex.py
output: HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found -- extracted --> ['404', 'Not Found'], reason: Not Found
output: HTTP/1.1 200 OK -- extracted --> ['200', 'OK'], reason: OK
output: HTTP/2 404 -- extracted --> ['404'], reason: Not Found
output: HTTP/2 200 -- extracted --> ['200'], reason: OK
```

## Comment (belforte, 2025-09-05T11:43:30Z)

thanks @Lorenzov1999 and @sinonkt !!
I do not think there ever was an intention not to be compliant with Http v2, but it is quite likely that when this code was written only Http v1 was around for testing.

merging

## Comment (belforte, 2025-09-05T11:55:36Z)

@Lorenzov1999 IIUC the problem was not "log is ugly" nor "console output is misleading" but "things do not work" !
Is that the case ?
If so.. why did we not catch in our tests ? are you using some new CMSSW release or non-standard environment ?

Besides curiosity, we need to know if to handle this as something to add to new release when we make it (we just deployed one this week and have no changes in the pipeline atm), or a critical bug to fix ASAP.

Thanks

## Comment (nausikt, 2025-09-05T12:24:54Z)

> @Lorenzov1999 IIUC the problem was not "log is ugly" nor "console output is misleading" but "things do not work" ! Is that the case ? If so.. why did we not catch in our tests ? are you using some new CMSSW release or non-standard environment ?
>

@belforte , To answer your Second and Third questions. (not sure whether this is the case)

`curl` we got, provisioned from CMSSW environment [1] are strictly HTTP/1.1 only. as you can check via `curl -V | grep -Eo 'HTTP2|HTTP3'`.
[1]
```
[kphornsi@lxplus909 CRABClient]$ which curl
/cvmfs/cms.cern.ch/el9_amd64_gcc12/cms/cmssw/CMSSW_14_0_20/external/el9_amd64_gcc12/bin/curl
```

On the other hand, `curl` on `lxplus` or my laptop in general. they support HTTP2 as default. as you can see in [2]

[2]
```
[kphornsi@lxplus909 ~]$ which curl
/usr/bin/curl
[kphornsi@lxplus909 ~]$ curl -V | grep -Eo 'HTTP2|HTTP3'
HTTP2
```

So, i guessed this might be the reasons why most of our tests passed because it's run in control env where there is specific `curl` underneath.

Yes @belforte, the issue was indeed a "things do not work", but I confirm that, as @sinonkt pointed out, this happened while using CRAB outside of any CMS env.

Thank you both for the quick response!

thanks @Lorenzov1999
I am amazed that CRAB could work outside CMS env (which indeeed is what we rely on to provide che python dependencies we have, among other things). I would expect that if $CMSSW* are not defined it fails miserably.
I will be very interested in knowing more about how you managed, maybe we can have an officially supported setup and add to our testing, at least for people using e.g. python3.

This is just an attempt for the moment, but, if it turns out to be successful, I will remember to get in touch and discuss this further.

@belforte

> Besides curiosity, we need to know if to handle this as something to add to new release when we make it (we just deployed one this week and have no changes in the pipeline atm), or a critical bug to fix ASAP.
